races.name: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
British EBF Novice Stakes

runners_data.name: Majestic Jude
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner with a going-fit profile on Good, but finished fifth on debut and is a genuine hold-up horse who, with rivals also preferring the rear, will struggle to find clear passage unless the pace is genuine enough to stretch the field.

runners_data.name: Moheebb
runners_data.note: John Butler's charge finished sixth on debut at this trip and going combination, and as a natural hold-up runner in a field where the pace is unlikely to be strong, faces an uphill task closing from behind in a slow-tempo sprint.

runners_data.name: Nidal
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends this runner back quickly (14 days) after finishing eighth last time, and the tagged fade in the finish is a significant concern given the likely steady gallop here will demand a sharp final-furlong effort he has yet to demonstrate.

runners_data.name: On Target
runners_data.note: George Scott's juvenile is the only confirmed pace-setter and should control the race from the front; though tagged as racing slightly out of natural role versus a deeper read, On Target's previous 4th and 6th suggest it handles this trip and going, and front-running freedom is a major tactical asset today.

runners_data.name: Al Jabbar
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby debutant partnered by Billy Loughnane — unknown style (U) but the yard's powerful 14-day record (12/27) and habitually well-prepared juveniles make this a live unknown; going fitness and racing style are both uncharted but the pedigree angle could be decisive.

runners_data.name: Astabuen
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's first-time starter with George Downing aboard is an entirely open book on style and going, and with a lower 14-day strike rate (4/42) than the Appleby rival, needs to show natural ability on debut to feature against even this modest level of form.

races.paceDynamic: On Target is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop down the Newmarket July Course straight. At Good to Firm conditions over 7f, that translates to a measured, controlled tempo that rewards horses able to travel prominently and produce a sustained finish rather than an explosive late burst. The debutants Al Jabbar and Astabuen are unknown tactical quantities and could complicate the shape, but absent evidence they carry genuine pace, On Target dictates. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the final two furlongs, making prominent-to-midfield runners who travel kindly the optimal profile. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the field can accommodate — Majestic Jude, Moheebb, and Nidal are all genuine hold-up horses, but with the pace scenario likely to be slow-to-moderate, those at the furthest back face the greatest challenge to close the gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Gallop, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If On Target dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the closers are held up too far back to reel in.
scenarios.body: On Target rolls along in front without pressure, and any horse able to track within two lengths of the leader through the final quarter-mile will have first run; the slow early tempo compresses the field and negates pure hold-up runners who need a true test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced debutants (Al Jabbar or Astabuen) shows unexpectedly strong form and powers through the field from midfield.
scenarios.body: Al Jabbar (Appleby/Loughnane, unbeaten yard at the top of their game) or Astabuen could carry a significant unknown ceiling and motor past beaten rivals in the final furlong; the moderate pace sets up a sprint finish that a raw but talented newcomer can exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than expected and On Target ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for trailing runners.
scenarios.body: Moheebb or Majestic Jude, if able to get closer than their natural hold-up roles typically allow, could benefit from a leader stopping in front of them; this shape requires a truer pace than the lone front-runner scenario suggests and is therefore unlikely in this small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race unfolds in a chaotic fashion due to debutant behaviour and the field splits tactically, exposing an unpredictable winner.
scenarios.body: With two first-time starters whose temperament and tactical awareness are entirely unknown, a fractured race shape could scramble the expected order; Nidal or Moheebb capitalise if the front fails to dominate and late closers catch a true gallop.

watchPoints.text: On Target — watch whether it meets any challenge from the two debutants in the early stages; if unopposed it could dictate to a degree that makes it very hard to pass in the straight.
Al Jabbar — Charlie Appleby's debutant is the chief unknown; watch the market moves pre-race, as this yard routinely introduces well-schooled juveniles ready to run to a high level first time.
Majestic Jude — despite being mapped to midfield, this is a true hold-up horse; if the pace is modest it may find itself with too much ground to make up at a track that rewards prominent running.
Nidal — the quick turnaround (14 days) and a fade-in-finish flag are worth noting; watch whether it travels smoothly early or already looks to be struggling before the final furlong begins.

Field compactness — with only 6 runners and a lone front-runner, watch whether the field bunches tightly turning into the straight, which could cause interference and favour the horse with the clearest run rather than the fastest finisher.

races.name: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: Won twice over 5f-6f on good ground and boasts solid course form; races prominently and should slot in just behind the pace battle, giving her a clear sighting run into the final furlong — her OR of 85 gives her a slight class edge over most rivals.|
runners_data.comment: Elara May has won twice in her last five starts, most recently scoring three runs back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — the worry is that eighth last time out leaves her form needing some explanation.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Primary hold-up exponent in the field, with recent good-ground course-distance form (1st and 3rd over 6f/Good), a live trainer in form (4/13, 14 days), and the profile best suited to the strong early pace this field guarantees — 35 days off is not a concern given that pattern in her history.|
runners_data.comment: Powdering arrives on the back of a third last time out, and a winner two starts back, giving her a decent recent profile, though she has been unplaced inside that sequence; has run over today's trip and going, and 135 lb from stall seven makes this a fair test.

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won twice on Soft/Standard and shown early pace on good ground; Billy Loughnane will look to break well and control tempo, but with Angel Shared and Bright Summer also wanting the lead, she faces a genuine three-way pace duel that may cost her in the closing stages.|
runners_data.comment: Zighy shaped well last time when runner-up, and her two recent wins in her last five starts underline genuine ability; she has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 84 marks her as a live threat, though 53 days off the track is the key question.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Races from rear to midfield and has placed four times over 6f on good going without winning in recent starts — the visor is retained, which is worth noting, and a distant 19th last time out on Good adds a question mark, though the two prior runs (2nd, 2nd) over 6f/Good show she belongs at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Shallow has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, with a second two runs back and thirds among her last six, and she has run over today's distance and going before; the concern is she remains winless in that spell and must convert placed efforts into something more.

runners_data.name: Angel Shared
runners_data.note: Veteran 5yo front-runner with three wins over this course-distance profile, though her recent form (9th, 4th, 6th, 13th) suggests she is finding it harder to dominate from the front; trainer at 0/12 in 14 days, and she will likely press the pace rather than control it.|
runners_data.comment: Angel Shared arrives on the back of a fourth two starts back and a third five starts back, yet to win in recent starts, though her rating of 87 — top of the eight, if only narrowly — marks her as the class act here, and her experience over today's trip and going is a genuine asset at 132 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Bright Summer
runners_data.note: Runs off the front and has been campaigned almost exclusively at 7f — dropping back to 6f for the first time is a genuine query, and her flat strike rate prominently (0W 0P in recent runs) suggests she could be exposed as the weakest of the three pace-setters once the 6f tempo bites.|
runners_data.comment: Bright Summer arrives on the back of two disappointing efforts after a win four starts back, and her recent unplaced finish is the concern; experience over today's trip and going at least offers some footing, but she faces a stiff task from stall three.

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent on good ground with five placed or winning efforts from recent starts, and her natural gate speed (two 5f wins, two places at 5f) means she can sit prominent just off the leaders and pounce — the question is whether 6f on Good to Firm stretches her stamina under a bigger weight (125lbs).|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the field on our figures and rated three pounds below her official mark, Adalida faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before, is drawn in stall one, and two wins in her last six starts show she can find the frame.

runners_data.name: Seeing Stars
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has placed twice on good ground at 7f; racing from a prominent-patient position, she drops back to 6f for the first time in recent runs which is a slight distance concern, but she is very freshly raced (10 days) and Harry Davies will aim to track the pace cleanly.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Seeing Stars has been out of the placings in her last two starts and faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before, returns on a quick turnaround of ten days, and draws stall two carrying 119 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Zighy, Angel Shared, and Bright Summer are all confirmed front-runners, meaning this 6f handicap at Newmarket's July course will be run at a genuine, unrelenting gallop from the outset — there will be no tactical dawdling. Adalida's profile also suggests prominent intent, compressing the early-position battle further and ensuring the pace is not only strong but potentially fierce, with leaders burning significant energy through the first two furlongs on what is Good to Firm ground. The three hold-up and midfield types — Powdering, Shallow, and Elara May — are poised to benefit structurally from this shape, as a hot early pace over 6f on a flat, fair track historically drags closers into play at the 2f pole. The pace dynamic here distinctly favours hold-up and midfield runners who can track the carnage and sustain a smooth late run, rather than any single front-runner who must both lead and repel challengers under the burden of a strongly-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Blows, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the contested lead between Zighy, Angel Shared, and Bright Summer generates a truly hot early pace that deflates the front rank in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace battle among three genuine front-runners is likely to leave all of them short of finishing speed in the closing stages, opening the door for Powdering and Shallow to produce sustained late runs up the Newmarket straight. Powdering's hold-up profile, recent course-distance form, and trainer's current strike rate (4/13 in 14 days) make her the primary beneficiary, with Shallow's prominent-from-rear style a strong secondary threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Zighy breaks sharply and dictates a controlled, measured gallop that takes the sting out of the pace battle and leaves her with a decisive kick.
scenarios.body: Zighy's best form has come when front-running at 6f on good ground (two Stan wins, course form solid), and if Billy Loughnane steals a march at the start she could dictate on her own terms without burning energy in a duel. A controlled lead on this flat course would give Zighy the sustained gallop she needs to hold on, and Adalida — likely sitting closest — becomes the primary challenger given her repeated second-place finishes on good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners neutralise each other early but Adalida or Elara May, racing prominently just off the pace, inherit the perfect stalking position.
scenarios.body: Adalida has finished first or second in five of her last six starts on good ground and her 5f-to-6f profile suggests she has the tactical speed to sit just behind a hot pace and quicken into it at the right moment. Elara May, whose best effort (1st, 5f, Good) shows she can produce a bold early move from a prominent pitch, also fits this shape if she times her run to the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually moderate or the closers suffer traffic and Powdering or Shallow are forced widest, leaving only a partial late run that falls fractionally short.
scenarios.body: A race at Newmarket over 6f on quick ground very rarely produces a slow early gallop with this many front-runners declared, making a genuine pace collapse unlikely; Shallow's visor (headgear) and inconsistent form string (19th most recently) adds uncertainty to whether she fully fires. This scenario edges toward Seeing Stars, who has placed at this course on good ground with a prominent-patient style, if she can secure a clean run from stall.

watchPoints.text: Powdering's ability to secure a clear run from her hold-up berth is critical — if Zighy, Angel Shared, and Bright Summer inject pace from the gate, Dylan Hogan must avoid getting trapped in a pocket inside the final 2f where Newmarket's straight offers little room to switch.|

Bright Summer is unproven at 6f having run all recent starts at 7f — if the drop in trip catches her out in the final furlong she could cause significant interference as a weakening front-runner, impeding Shallow or Powdering finishing hard on her outside.|

The three-way early duel between Zighy, Angel Shared, and Bright Summer could produce a breakneck early split time — watch the sectional pace through the first 2f, as any significant overcooking there effectively eliminates all three from winning calculations and turns this into a closers' race.|

Adalida's consistency on good ground is notable but her stamina at 6f on Good to Firm (all her best form over 5f) is an open question — if she is outpaced and drops off in the final furlong rather than sustaining, Callum Shepherd may struggle to recover ground on this flat, unforgiving track.|

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's stablemate concern aside — Jim & Suzi Best's 1/11 trainer form over 14 days is tepid — Liberate is a genuine hold-up horse whose best recent effort came over 13f at Good and needs a strongly-run race to produce his finishing effort; this sedate pace is unlikely to serve him.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of five on our ratings, Liberate carries a workable weight from stall two and has run over today's trip, giving her a fitness edge at 24 days fresh; the risk is that she has been winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Fanciulla Del West
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly has recent placed form at 10f and 12f on Good and brings the single most important asset in this field: total control of the pace from the front, with no rival willing or able to press her early; the 50-day absence is the only meaningful query.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and twice runner-up in recent starts, Fanciulla Del West shaped well before an unplaced effort last time, and she has experience over today's trip and going to call on; yet to win in her last five, but rated highest of the five runners, she shapes as the one to beat from stall four.

runners_data.name: Emma's Letter
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rode her to a 10f win on Good and she steps back to 10f having found 12f too far; the tongue tie is noted and she carries hold-up tendencies that put her at a disadvantage unless Fanciulla Del West sets a true gallop — Ed Dunlop's 1/17 14-day strike rate is modest.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, Emma's Letter brings solid recent form into this, has experience of today's trip and going, and 133 lb from stall one is the chief impost to overcome.

runners_data.name: Miss Guinevere
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes has 3/13 over 14 days which is solid, but this filly's natural instinct is to race from the rear — she has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map only because the hold-up section is crowded, and her three career starts include two poor efforts at 8f on Good/Soft; stepping up in trip is the only encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Miss Guinevere faces a stiff task here; the 64-day absence is a concern, though she has run over today's going before and stall three is a neutral draw.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's yard is in reasonable form at 5/35 over 14 days and Port Darwin brings two wins from fifteen on similar going, most recently scoring over 10f on Good; his prominent style is the best fit for tracking Fanciulla Del West and striking from close range, and the 16-day freshener looks ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Port Darwin won last time out and also took a win four starts back, bringing two wins in his last six starts, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the worry is that consecutive fifth-placed efforts two and three starts back suggest consistency remains a question.

races.paceDynamic: Fanciulla Del West is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push her early, she is likely to control proceedings at a measured, comfortable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Newmarket's July course. Port Darwin holds prominent-race credentials and will likely sit just behind her in second, meaning the pace is set by one horse with a single chaser rather than a contested duel — a recipe for a sustainable tempo that rewards those who travel well into the race. Miss Guinevere is a genuine hold-up type who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field's rear is not as congested as it appears; in reality she will likely race closer to the tail than her mapped position suggests, meaning the true hold-up spot is occupied by Liberate and Emma's Letter. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a fair but not searching gallop — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel within striking range and pounce in the final two furlongs, with Fanciulla Del West herself able to steal a march if the pursuit is slow to react.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fanciulla Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Fanciulla Del West dictates an unchallenged pace and the field fails to reel her in entering the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Fanciulla Del West sets a confident, unhurried tempo with Port Darwin tracking, and when she kicks two furlongs out the field lacks the early position to bridge the gap in time on this fast ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Port Darwin Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Port Darwin tracks Fanciulla Del West closely and produces a strong, sustained challenge from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Port Darwin's recent course and distance win at 10f on Good gives him the profile to outstay the leader from a stalking berth, with Callum Shepherd timing the challenge to peak close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to stop the leaders and Emma's Letter or Liberate close strongly from the rear.
scenarios.body: Emma's Letter brings a win at 10f on Good and has the class to overhaul a tiring leader if the tempo bites, while Liberate needs a thorough end-to-end gallop that this pace configuration is unlikely to deliver.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Miss Guinevere Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Guinevere overcomes her limited recent form and races more prominently than expected to take advantage of a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: Her redistribution note signals she is a true hold-up type racing out of role here, and with only three runs to her name on soft and standard she is exposed as the least likely beneficiary of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Fanciulla Del West — watch whether George Downing allows her to bowl along at her own pace unchallenged from the outset; if she gets a soft lead through the first half-mile she could prove very hard to catch on Good to Firm ground.

Port Darwin — Callum Shepherd's positioning in the first furlong is critical; if he slots in directly behind Fanciulla Del West rather than drifting wide, he is best placed to deliver a challenge and must be tracked closely.

Emma's Letter — the tongue tie is first-time headgear and can produce unpredictable early behaviour; watch her at the start and in the first furlong, as a slow break from this hold-up profile would leave her with far too much ground to make up.

Miss Guinevere — her 64-day absence and limited form at shorter distances means any early signs of greenness or reluctance to settle should be noted; she is the most unexposed runner but also the least proven for this trip and tempo.

Liberate — 24 days since last run is fresh but not concerning; the key watch point is whether he gets cover in the rear group and whether the pace is strong enough to bring him into contention in the final furlong, which on current evidence looks unlikely.

races.name: End Of Summer Season Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rizal
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f-12f on Good ground recently and the step back up to 1m4f looks entirely within range; Billy Loughnane takes over and will likely adopt front-running tactics, though the [STYLE_FIT] flag means that if the race demands he overpaces himself to hold off closers, his chance narrows.|
runners_data.comment: Rizal has won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and he arrives with experience of both today's trip and going — a thoroughly relevant profile. The main risk is 35 days off the track, leaving his current sharpness to prove.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin's booking gives a polish to a horse with consistent placed form at 12f on Good and similar going, and he handles this trip well — though his natural style is deep hold-up, here he will likely find himself in a closer midfield berth than ideal given the race shape, which is neither his preferred slot nor his worst.|
runners_data.comment: Patrol arrives here in solid fitness after a run 27 days ago and has experience of today's distance and going, with a third two starts back and a second four starts back in recent form; rated 86 by us and the top-ranked of the four, he looks the one to beat despite being winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Parisian Scholar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's charge arrives on the back of back-to-back 12f wins on Good ground and his form profile fits this race beautifully — a genuine hold-up type comfortable sitting last and producing a late run on fast ground at exactly this trip, and the 21-day gap looks sharp enough.|
runners_data.comment: Parisian Scholar arrives on the back of back-to-back wins earlier in this sequence and returns fit on 21 days' rest, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the risk is that two unplaced efforts since those successes leave his current form under a question mark.

runners_data.name: Zurna
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good ground last time and placed at 10f on similar, making this trip and going squarely in her wheelhouse; Dylan Hogan has a light book and will likely settle her deep before asking for her effort in the straight, and the 43-day absence is the one mild note of caution.|
runners_data.comment: Zurna arrives on the back of back-to-back placed efforts culminating in a win last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the chief concern is that 43 days off the track leaves a fitness question hanging over him heading into this contest.

races.paceDynamic: Rizal is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of four over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course, and with no other horse likely to press for the lead, he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Patrol, though a natural hold-up type, has been redistributed to a midfield position on the map simply because the rear is occupied by genuine closers; in reality Patrol will try to settle deep alongside Parisian Scholar and Zurna. With just one pace-setter setting what figures to be a modest, uncontested tempo, the race sets up as a test of finishing speed rather than relentless front-running stamina, meaning the closing burst from the trio tracking behind will determine everything in the straight. This shape strongly favours the hold-up runners who can quicken off a comfortable gallop — Parisian Scholar and Zurna in particular, both of whom carry recent winning form at this sort of trip and going — while Rizal, racing slightly out of his natural lead role, may find the steady pace ultimately plays into the hands of those with the sharper finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Rizal sets a modest, uncontested pace and the hold-up trio track smoothly before unleashing finishing kicks in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Rizal's controlled gallop keeps the race at a measured tempo all the way to the home turn, and the lack of any rival to force genuine early pressure means the closers arrive with energy intact; Parisian Scholar and Zurna, both recent winners on similar going and trip, are ideally placed to deliver the decisive finishing move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Rizal dictates a strategically slow early pace then kicks decisively turning in, stretching the field before closers can organise.
scenarios.body: Rizal's rider Billy Loughnane, experienced enough to exploit a thin field, could slow the race to a crawl and produce an extended sprint from well out, catching the hold-up horses flat-footed; his recent winning form at 10f-12f on Good ground suggests he retains enough scope to last home if the run-in becomes a straight gallop rather than a sustained test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Patrol, settled slightly closer than his true preference, produces a sustained grinding effort to outlast the sharper types.
scenarios.body: Patrol's 0-for-15 strike rate is a concern, but his consistent placed record at 12f on Good and Good to Soft suggests he stays well and could benefit if the sharp finishers fail to quicken cleanly; this scenario depends on conditions that make finishing speed irrelevant and raw stamina the decider, which is the least likely outcome on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jockeys refuse to be led and the pace becomes dangerously slow, creating a sprint finish that suits an unexpected profile.
scenarios.body: A four-runner field with one genuine leader and three nominal hold-up types can occasionally produce tactical chaos if no horse wants to commit from the front, turning 1m4f into a long-distance sprint; in that extreme scenario the most adaptable jockey wins, but this remains a very unlikely outcome given Rizal's confirmed willingness to lead.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rizal's early splits — if Billy Loughnane softens the gallop dramatically through the first half-mile, the hold-up trio will have all the time they need to close and Rizal's chance of lasting home diminishes sharply.

Parisian Scholar has beaten similar rivals over this exact trip and going twice running; if Callum Shepherd times the challenge to hit the front inside the final furlong, he is the most dangerous closer in the field.
Zurna's 43-day absence means fitness is a slight question mark — if she needs the run she may not fire her full finishing kick, which would leave the scenario hinging on Parisian Scholar alone.

With only four runners and one genuine pace-setter, the risk of a falsely-run race that becomes a sprint in the final quarter-mile is real — any horse that drifts wide turning into the Newmarket straight will concede critical ground in a small field.

races.name: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rogue Citation
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 7f on her most recent start and wore headgear (hg:t) suggesting she needs to switch on; Harry Davies keeps her prominent at Newmarket where the straight 7f suits organised, rail-hugging runners, and her 14-day freshness is a positive — key danger if she slots in cleanly behind the leaders.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Citation won last time out and her trainer is firing at 36% over the past fortnight, so she arrives in cracking order; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 135 lb from stall six is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Splash
runners_data.note: Has a strong recent win over this exact course and distance on Good, though four of her last five runs at this trip on Good produced a 14th, 9th, and 6th — the one win excepted; Robert Havlin will need a clear passage from her hold-up position after 37 days off, and she needs the pace duel to be genuine.
runners_data.comment: She matches her official mark on our figures but ranks seventh of nine, making her hard to fancy in this company despite a win in her last five starts; she does have experience of today's trip and going, and 37 days between runs suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Miss Gallant
runners_data.note: Two-run form string conceals a confident winner on her most recent start at 7f on Standard; wears headgear (hg:h) and breaks as a confirmed front-runner — Jack Gilligan will look to establish her immediately and the 47-day break is the only question against a horse who has won both career starts.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Miss Gallant faces a stiff ask at 132 lb from stall nine, and a speed rating of 61 underlines the concern; the trainer's sharp 26% strike rate and her winning return last time out are the genuine positives, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Too Too Divine
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Good most recently and steps back to 7f where her best form is a third on Soft — James Fanshawe's yard is in decent 14-day form and George Wood rides a horse who wants to be prominent; the extra furlong and Good to Firm ground are slight concerns but her recent win suggests confidence.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Too Too Divine faces a stiff task, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's distance and going to her name.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: The most exposed prominent runner in the field with six career runs, three wins at 7f, and strong Good-ground form; Callum Hutchinson rides a horse trained by Andrew Balding whose operation is in excellent 14-day shape — the contested lead with Miss Gallant is the main risk as neither is likely to yield.
runners_data.comment: Allegrino ran second last time out and has shown a consistent profile across her last six starts, with two wins in that span; she has experience over today's trip and going, but 130 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: Carries the highest weight at 130lbs alongside Allegrino and arrives 44 days fresh with a form string of 43588 that shows a sharp drop in level; a genuine prominent type by nature, Ironist is squeezed back to a mapped midfield role by the congestion ahead of her, and that racing out of her natural position significantly tempers her chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Ironist has shown ability — a third four starts back — but her recent pair of eighths cloud the picture, and she heads here winless in her last five starts after a 44-day break; experience over today's trip and going offers some hope from stall five carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Hilltop
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount is a five-year-old carrying the race-top 140lbs and has placed at 7f on Good before — the weight and the prominent traffic are the double headwind here; Daniel & Claire Kubler are in modest 14-day form and Hilltop's four career runs at this trip suggest she needs things to fall right from a prominent position she may not secure.
runners_data.comment: Hilltop shaped well for third three starts back and was a winner four starts back, so there is clear ability here; drawn in stall one and carrying 140 lb on a quick turnaround of 14 days, the weight ask is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Bami
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's filly won over this exact 7f Good track on her most recent start and returns after 59 days — the freshness and proven form on this course and surface give her strong credentials; Pierre-Louis Jamin rides a prominent-style horse who will need to navigate the early scrimmage to land in a clean position by the time the race settles.
runners_data.comment: Bami shaped as a genuine threat here, winning last time out and a winner three starts back too, and she has experience of both today's trip and going; the main concern is a 59-day absence since that last success.

runners_data.name: Ghisa
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes runner wears headgear (hg:h) and has not won in seven career starts, with her best recent efforts a pair of thirds on Standard going — Paddy Bradley will have her held up from the back but 0 wins and 0 places on Good in similar-going runs is a sobering statistic that makes this a tough ask even if the pace suits.
runners_data.comment: Placed third in each of her last two starts, Ghisa arrives in fine recent nick and, with experience over today's trip and a rating of 89 topping the nine runners, she looks the one to beat here, though a first win remains elusive in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Gallant and Allegrino are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates, creating an honest, competitive gallop on Good to Firm ground over this 7f Rowley Mile layout. With Rogue Citation, Too Too Divine, Hilltop, and Bami all wanting prominent positions, there will be significant scrimmaging for the first two furlongs as four runners chase two slots, raising real traffic and interference risk between the 2f and 3f markers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Miss Gallant and Allegrino are likeliest to actually lead, with Rogue Citation best placed to grab the rail slot behind them and Hilltop potentially shuffled back from where she wants to be. This race shape — a genuine, front-pressed pace with prominent congestion — will stretch the field early and suit a horse travelling smoothly in the first three, giving prominent-to-midfield horses who can save ground the decisive late advantage as the pace-setters tie each other up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Gallant and Allegrino fight it out up front and burn enough petrol that the winner comes from just off the pace in the first two
scenarios.body: The contested lead sets a genuine gallop that sees the front two fade inside the final furlong, handing the race to a horse that travelled smoothly in third or fourth and picked up off the bend; 7f on Good to Firm at Newmarket rewards stamina-tinged prominent types who get a tow

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Miss Gallant — breaks best and gets a comfortable lead while the other checks or settles
scenarios.body: The leader controls the fractions, keeps them manageable and maintains enough in the tank to resist challengers in the final 1f; Newmarket's straight 7f suits a horse that can bowl along without being headed and quicken again at the death

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is truly strong and the field compresses late, allowing a hold-up horse to weave through and catch the tiring leaders
scenarios.body: Splash and Ghisa would need a clear run between 2f and 1f out to unleash their late kicks, and a strongly-run race would play to their staying ability; both have fair form at 7f on Good, though their hold-up style depends on a generous gallop they cannot manufacture themselves

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Traffic Incident
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion between the 2f and 3f markers causes a significant check, bump, or interference that reshapes the field mid-race
scenarios.body: A horse who finds daylight early or avoids the scrimmage altogether would emerge clear while others lose momentum; this scenario is low-probability but the density of prominent types makes it a genuine structural risk in this field

watchPoints.text: Watch Miss Gallant and Allegrino at the gates — if both break sharply and neither yields, the contested lead could become a genuine burn-up that compromises both their chances inside the final furlong.

Prominent congestion involving Rogue Citation, Too Too Divine, Hilltop, and Bami in the first 2f creates a high-risk scrimmage — any horse caught wide or checked early will lose multiple lengths at a critical stage on this straight track.
Bami's 59-day absence is the longest in the field — watch her post-race for signs of blowing, and note that Tom Dascombe's yard has only one winner from ten runners in the last 14 days.

Ironist's effective mapping to midfield means Callum Shepherd must ride her out of her natural prominent role — watch whether she settles and travels or becomes restless behind horses she would normally be alongside.

Splash's jumping of the stall and early position will be telling — if Robert Havlin gets her rolling smoothly from the hold-up position, her win here over this course and trip on Good is live form; if she gets boxed in early she has no ability to manufacture her own pace.
